about: The rocket's lift-off across the harbour (data/motion/launch.json: the engines light 1 s into the stage's time, the rocket lifts at 4 s and climbs at its push of 24 m/s/s against 9.81). The game 2099 never draws this rocket leaving its pad (the player rides it), so nothing here is the game's: every effect is modelled on real footage of a lift-off at night (the footage block's sources, NASA's photographs of Falcon Heavy at LC-39A), many fine particles tied to the world: the flame under the rocket and its hot exhaust spreading over the pad, the ground cloud of exhaust and steam rolling out sideways from the pad, the deluge's steam rising round it, the trail of exhaust the rocket leaves as it climbs, and the flame's light on the pad, the clouds and the harbour. The pad has no flame trench, so the exhaust spreads from the pad every way round rather than out of one side as at LC-39A; the measures are in the rocket's heights (60 m here, about 70 m for Falcon Heavy).

effects.name: flame_core
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013 (the white core of the flame under the cores, about a fifth of the rocket's height)

effects.name: flame
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013, KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046 (the orange flame, half to one rocket height long under the rocket, widening as it goes)

effects.name: pad_fire
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010 (the hot exhaust glowing as it spreads over the pad round the rocket's foot, from the engines' start until the flame lifts clear); it glows on round the pad's foot at least 3.4 s past lift-off: the STP-2 sequence's last frame near the pad, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0016, was taken 3.38 s after KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004 at lift-off (01:20:28.34 against 01:20:24.96, the EXIF SubSecDateTimeOriginal of NASA's images)

effects.name: ground_cloud
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013, KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0036, KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046 (the exhaust and steam rolling out sideways from the pad in billows from ignition, one to two rocket heights out and up within seconds of lift-off, three and more a few seconds later, lingering long after)

effects.name: cloud_billows
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013, KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046 (the billows the exhaust throws up as it rolls out, the cloud standing near a rocket height within seconds of lift-off and two later)

effects.name: deluge_steam
effects.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004, KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046 (white steam rising round the pad's foot where the deluge's water meets the exhaust)

effects.name: plume
effects.from: footage: KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013 (the column of exhaust the rocket leaves under it as it climbs, thin and pale, lit by the flame near its top)

lights.name: flame_light
lights.from: footage: KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010, KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013 (the flame lights the pad, the tower and the clouds round it warm orange, and is given back by the water in front)

footage.how: Measured by eye on each photograph's pixels against the rocket's own length in it (Falcon Heavy, about 70 m), to roughly a sixth: the cloud's width and height, the flame under the rocket, the size of the smallest billows. The times after lift-off are read off the sequence of each launch's photographs.

KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004.what: Falcon Heavy STP-2 lifting off LC-39A at night, 25 June 2019, the moment of lift-off
KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0004.measured: rocket 270 px; the cloud out of the trench 300 px wide by 210 px high (1.1 by 0.8 rocket heights); low steam either side of the pad's foot about 0.2 rocket heights high; the apron round the flame lit orange well above the floodlit tower

KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010.what: the same launch, about two seconds after lift-off
KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0010.measured: rocket 215 px; the trench's cloud 345 by 340 px (1.6 by 1.6 rocket heights); the flame's glowing exhaust round the pad 225 px across and 95 px high (1.0 by 0.45); flame under the rocket about 0.55 rocket heights

KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013.what: the same launch, about three seconds after lift-off
KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0013.measured: rocket 230 px; the trench's cloud 375 by 395 px (1.6 by 1.7 rocket heights); the cloud round the pad 385 px across and about 110 px high (1.7 by 0.5); flame 0.67 rocket heights, its white core about a fifth; the smallest billows about 10 to 40 px (0.05 to 0.15 of the cloud's width)

KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0016.what: the same launch, 3.38 s after lift-off by the EXIF times (01:20:28.34 against _0004's 01:20:24.96)
KSC-20190625-PH_CSH01_0016.measured: the rocket about one of its heights up the tower; the exhaust round the pad's foot still glowing orange-white either side of the tower, the flame reaching down into it

KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0036.what: Falcon Heavy's demonstration flight from LC-39A by day, 6 February 2018, at lift-off
KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0036.measured: rocket 130 px; the cloud 330 by 165 px (2.5 by 1.3 rocket heights), billowing in many small lumps

KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046.what: the same flight about twelve seconds after lift-off
KSC-20180206-PH_KLS02_0046.measured: against the tower: the cloud round the pad about 1 to 2 rocket heights high and reaching about 3 out from the pad; the trench's cloud 4 to 5 high; the flame about one rocket height; a thin pale column of exhaust under the rocket
